clauses.reason: Terminated by Executive Order 12292 (signed February 23, 1981), section 10(b) of which revokes Executive Order 9799 of November 8, 1946. Section 11 of Executive Order 12292 states that it is effective as of February 15, 1981, which is therefore the effective date of the revocation; the alternative reading is that the revocation operated from signing on 1981-02-23 or publication on 1981-02-25. February 15, 1981 is also the date the Foreign Service Act of 1980 took effect (section 2403(a)), repealing the 1946 Act whose section 411 power the order delegated; section 2401(a) of the 1980 Act continued orders issued under the 1946 Act until revoked or superseded, so the repeal by itself did not end the order and the express revocation is the end. The order authorized and directed the Secretary of State to exercise the President's power under section 411 of the Foreign Service Act of 1946 to classify chief-of-mission positions into four classes, effective November 13, 1946. The label EO 9452 attached to one acting record in the dossier is the Federal Register issue holding Executive Order 12292, not an earlier revoking order.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (11 FR, November 13, 1946) is Executive Order 9799 signed November 8, 1946 (read in full). Inventory read and confirmed: one delegating clause with its effective-date sentence. End: Executive Order 12292 section 10(b), effective as of February 15, 1981 under its section 11; the Foreign Service Act of 1980 (public law 96-465, held in the source-ladder queue text) repealed the 1946 Act effective the same day (section 2205 with section 2403(a)) but continued issued orders until revoked or superseded (section 2401(a)), which is why the revocation, not the repeal, is claimed as the end. This closes the gap noted in prior research. Prior research: two earlier Astra claim versions for this order differ on later_events and neither is canonical; their reported gap (actual repeal, savings and effective-date terms of the 1980 Act) is addressed here. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog, all complete.

savings.reason: Executive Order 12292 contains no saving clause for this order, but section 2(c) of that order treats section 401 of the Foreign Service Act of 1980 as the replacement for section 411 of the 1946 Act, and section 2401(a) of the 1980 Act continued determinations and orders made under the 1946 Act until modified, revoked or superseded. Classifications of chief-of-mission positions made under the delegation are accrued consequences; the delegation itself ended with the revocation.
